name: Strawberry makeup

card.summary: A social-media makeup look built on flushed pink-red cheeks, glossy lips and light freckles for a fresh, youthful face.
card.note: A style trend with no formal definition; product allergies are the main cosmetic consideration.

quick.overview:
Strawberry makeup is a popular makeup look associated with TikTok. It centres on a dewy base, rosy-red blush on the cheeks and nose, glossy lips and sometimes faux freckles, giving a fresh, flushed appearance.

The payoff is a youthful, warm-toned face. It is a cosmetic styling choice that works through colour placement and sheen on the face, and beauty brands describe it as suiting all skin tones.
quick.how: People build the look with a sheer base or tinted serum, cream and powder blush in pink and red layered on the cheeks, nose bridge and temples, glossy lips, mascara and optional freckles drawn with brown gel liner. Details vary by creator.
quick.risks: Standard cosmetic considerations apply: product allergies and hygiene of shared tools and brushes. No studies have examined the look itself.

lead: Strawberry makeup, also called strawberry girl makeup, is a makeup trend that spread on TikTok in 2023 as a food-inspired look alongside latte makeup and glazed-donut skin.[1] Its palette takes its cue from the fruit: pink and red flushed cheeks, shiny red-pink lips and a glowy, luminous complexion.[1]

People use it to create a youthful, sun-warmed look. Blush placed on the cheeks, nose bridge and temples mimics a natural flush, and gloss and highlighter add shine that makes the face appear fresh and soft.[1][2] W magazine credited Hailey Bieber with turning the look into a trend, and quoted makeup artist Pat McGrath on how to achieve it.[2] No studies of the look have been published.

chain: Rosy blush across cheeks and nose
angle.text: The look uses layered blush, gloss and optional freckles to give the face a warm, flushed appearance, in a way beauty brands describe as natural rather than glam.

infobox: Rosy blush, glossy lips, dewy skin, faux freckles

paras: L'Oreal Paris describes the look as fresh, natural and flirty rather than glam, with glowy skin, flushed cheeks, red and pink on the lids and lips, optional faux freckles and shimmery cheekbones.[1] The brand says the look suits all skin tones.[1]
W magazine's description is of a dewy, rose-tinted flush that looks as though the wearer has spent the day in the sun, and contrasts it with the nude-and-brown latte trend.[2]

Beauty guides generally start with a lightweight base such as a buildable foundation or a tinted serum for skin-like coverage.[1] A soft matte pink blush is swept along the cheekbones, then a red-pink satin blush layered at the centre of the cheeks and, optionally, across the nose bridge.[1] Brown gel eyeliner can be dotted over cheeks and nose to imitate freckles, followed by highlighter, mascara and a pink or red gloss or balm.[1]

W magazine's version recommends cream blush on the places sunlight would naturally hit, namely the cheeks, nose bridge and temples, with a touch on the eyes and lips and several complementary shades for dimension; for cooler months it suggests setting the balm lightly with powder to soften the dewy finish.[2]

The look is discussed mainly in mainstream beauty content, where it is positioned as a way to appear younger and fresher. It sits alongside other cosmetic trends that rely on colour placement rather than skin treatment.

timeline.event: Strawberry girl makeup spreads on TikTok; W magazine publishes its feature on 28 August, crediting Hailey Bieber with the trend.[1][2]
W magazine updates its guide on 20 February, adding a fall variation.[2]
